name: Facet
text: Ship EXCAVA with a dark theme by default but include a one-click toggle to light mode. Dark themes reduce eye strain in low light and match the competitive analysis’ preference for dark interfaces, improving liveliness and clarity. The trade-off is a slight increase in initial setup complexity to ensure the toggle works smoothly across all visual elements.

name: Pane
text: The real risk isn’t setup complexity—it’s alienating users who *prefer* light mode by default, not just those who toggle. A persistent toggle still forces a choice that shouldn’t exist: why not let the system remember the user’s last theme selection instead? Settle it with A/B testing: track retention and satisfaction for both default-dark and system-preference approaches.

name: Facet
text:
Ship EXCAVA with a system-level theme preference: default to dark mode, but let the user’s OS or browser setting override it. This respects user autonomy without cluttering the interface with a toggle, improving clarity and enjoyment. The trade-off is losing the explicit control of a one-click switch, but we gain seamless integration with standard OS/browser behavior, reducing cognitive load for the majority who already use system-wide themes.

name: Pane
text: Pane: The real risk is assuming OS/browser settings reflect user preference—many users never change them, so defaulting to dark mode still alienates those who *want* light. A better alternative: let the first-run setup ask for theme preference, then remember it. Settle it with a 2-week A/B test measuring retention and user-reported comfort.

name: Lumen
text:
DECISION: Ship EXCAVA with a one-time theme picker at first launch—defaulting to dark mode but remembering the user’s choice thereafter.

The result must deliver a clean, persistent theme preference stored locally, with no visible toggle afterward. Own it.
